title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 60-61 of the 'Longue Marche' notes). L is a function field of transcendence degree n over K. On the previous page Grothendieck recovers the fundamental group π1(U) of a model U from the Galois group of L. It is the quotient by the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups I_V. Here V runs over the discrete valuation rings O_{U,x} at codimension-1 points x of U.

He then introduces the locally ringed space 𝒳_{L/K} = lim← X, the limit over proper models X of L/K. This is the Zariski–Riemann space ('abstract Riemann surface') of L/K. Points of 'codimension d' have residue fields of transcendence degree n−d. There is a unique generic point.

On this page:
(1) The codimension-1 points correspond, via x ↦ O_{𝒳,x}, to the valuations ('jauges') of L that are essentially of finite type over K. These are the divisorial DVRs, i.e. the V of the previous page.
(2) 'Sauf erreur', the generic point and these divisorial points are the only points whose local ring is noetherian. Together these two types exhaust 𝒳 when n=1, where 𝒳 is the regular proper curve and hence a scheme.
(3) Proposition: every O_{𝒳,x} is a valuation ring of L containing K with fraction field L. The map x ↦ O_{𝒳,x} is a bijection from 𝒳 onto the set of all such valuation rings. This is Zariski's theorem identifying the Zariski–Riemann space with the space of valuations of L/K.

Proof sketch, part a): given f ∉ O_{𝒳,x}, show 1/f ∈ O_{𝒳,x}. Write f = g/h with g, h ∈ O_{X,x} on some projective model X. By resolution, one may take X regular with g and h monomials in a regular system of parameters (times units). Further blowing up makes the divisors of g and h separate, i.e. one divides the other. This is continued on p. 61. Part b) on p. 61 begins the injectivity/surjectivity argument using centres of a valuation on each model.

Role: this prepares a 'birational' description of the inertia/decomposition structure for the anabelian programme. The fundamental groups of all models are seen as quotients of Gal(L̄/L) by inertia groups indexed by points of the Zariski–Riemann space.
errors: The 'sauf erreur' claim (2) is false for n ≥ 2. A valuation ring is noetherian iff it is a field or a DVR. But L/K has non-divisorial DVRs: rank 1, value group Z, with residue field of transcendence degree < n−1. Example: on K(x,y), take v(P) = ord_t P(t, e^t) (any transcendental power series instead of e^t). Its residue field is K, so it is not divisorial, yet its valuation ring is a DVR. Thus the points with noetherian local ring are the generic point and all DVR points, not only the divisorial ones.

The use of resolution of singularities in the proof of the valuation property is unnecessary if 𝒳 is defined as the limit over all proper (possibly singular) models, as Zariski did. To get g | h or h | g, it suffices to blow up the ideal (g,h), or take the closure of the graph of f. Resolution only matters if one restricts to regular models, as Grothendieck's NB on the previous page acknowledges.
The parenthetical about which n make 𝒳 a scheme is garbled in transcription and probably also in the manuscript. 𝒳 is a scheme for n ≤ 1 (for n=1 it is the regular proper curve), not only for n = 0.

ideas.what: Inverse limit of all proper models of a function field as a locally ringed space whose points correspond to valuation rings of L/K
ideas.usually_credited_to: O. Zariski (1940s), Zariski–Samuel vol. II; later Temkin and others
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA as such; EGA II §7 treats valuative criteria. Unsure about other texts.

ideas.what: Codimension-1 points ↔ divisorial valuations (essentially of finite type over K), the same V whose inertia groups give π1 of models
ideas.modern_name: divisorial valuations / prime divisors on birational models

ideas.what: Proof of the valuation property via monomialization by resolution plus further blow-ups to separate divisors

deep.surprise_reason: This is Grothendieck re-deriving the classical Zariski–Riemann space and Zariski's bijection with valuation rings, as a tool for the birational/anabelian setting. It is standard material. It even contains a small error (non-divisorial DVRs are overlooked) and an unnecessary reliance on resolution. Nothing new beyond the motivation of linking it to inertia groups, which is already implicit in birational anabelian work (Pop, Bogomolov).
transcription_corrections: Previous page end/first line: the points described are almost certainly 'codim 1' points (corresponding to divisorial valuations), not 'codim 2'.
Proof line: 'f = g/h, g,h ∈ O_{X,x}' — the subscript is the model X, not 𝒳. Later 'f, g' should read 'g, h' (the numerator and denominator), made monomial in a regular system of parameters.
'OPS ∃ syst. régulier de paramètres' = 'On peut supposer qu'il existe un système régulier de paramètres'.
